eps_hi_clipping_policy.rule: Never clip eps_hi for arithmetic or certification. Store and print eps_hi_raw, store a separate display-clipped value, compute floor=max(0,(1-eps_hi_raw)/2), and mark certificate-lost or alphabet-invalid.

design_vs_empirical_note: All rows are design-time synthetic ensemble calculations using known true channel TV values and registered compression factors. A real-data run must replace known true TV by empirical tv_hat on the fixed pre-registered grid; no row here is an empirical traffic result.
realizability_assumption: Every divisibility number assumes independent iid samples and that the selected classifier family contains, or sufficiently approximates, a useful binary rejection test for the pair. The held-out Clopper-Pearson witness is conditional on the learned classifier; this route is assumption-laden and not distribution-free.
known_limitations: The synthetic pair law occupies three fixed cells while the upper-side m is the full fixed a-priori grid.
The classifier route is the one-hot Michel construction used by the ladder; the divisibility route receives the identical sampled cell IDs directly.
The classifier lower route is an asymptotic HPLB, not an exact finite-sample certificate.
The divisibility route has a finite-sample held-out binomial construction conditional on the learned test, but requires realizability and is not distribution-free.
The ten pair levels, compression factors, and sample sizes are design-time choices and cannot establish real-corpus pair distributions.
The comparison changes lower-bound tightness, not the verdict form: upper-side feasibility still uses raw eps_hi and the lower-side reachability condition remains compression_factor > T(n).
blockers: No real per-service pair distributions were supplied; the report cannot answer the empirical traffic verdict.
